chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked him about a man who broke his fast for one day from the month of Ramadan deliberately. He said: He should give in charity twenty Sa's and he should make up for it.

key_terms.صَاعاً: Sa' (a unit of volume for dry goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the kaffarah for deliberately breaking the fast in Ramadan, requiring the payment of twenty Sa's of food in charity alongside making up the missed day (qada). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often discussed in contrast to the Hanafi view of a single kaffarah, highlighting the distinct Shia emphasis on both expiation and restitution for the specific act of intentional nullification.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who breaks a Fast of a day from the Month of Ramazan, deliberately. He<sup>asws</sup>: ‘He should give in charity with twenty Sa’a, and he should fulfil (another Fast) in its place’.
en.sarwar: 8. Humayd ibn Yazid has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who destroys his fast in the month of Ramadan purposely.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to give twenty Sa‘ in charity and make Qada’ (compensatory fast) that fast.’”
